propositions: When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, blocked sessions see only a bare pid and cannot determine if interrupting the holder is safe.
The code already knows the holder is a compaction sweep and that interrupting it is lossless, but this information does not reach the operator's error message.
Lock timeout errors should name the holder operation (e.g., 'compact-sweep') and state that it is safe to interrupt, enabling operators to self-serve rather than manually kill unknown processes.
An ambient contextvars-based operation label mechanism should propagate from sweep entry points to lock acquisition without modifying acquisition call sites or compact_txn.py.
The lock owner stamp must remain colon-free for forward compatibility while adding an optional sanitized op=field that is appended by _owner_stamp and rendered in timeout messages.
Staleness and reclamation logic must remain label-blind so that labeled and unlabeled stale locks adjudicate identically.
